verdict_word: Profit beat, revenue miss: gold prices did the lifting, mines delivered less
takeaways: Revenue rose 13% to $549.3 million on higher gold and oil prices, but precious-metal deliveries were 'slightly below expectations,' per CEO Paul Brink in the company release.
GEOs sold fell 6% to 130,435 on lower contributions from Guadalupe-Palmarejo, Antapaccay and Cobre Panama; Reuters said revenue missed on lower gold stream deliveries.
Net income rose 38% to $395.5 million ($2.05 a share), helped by items excluded from adjusted earnings, including a partial Cobre Panama impairment reversal (Business News Today).
Panama's interministerial commission recommended formal negotiations with First Quantum over Cobre Panama's future; no restart has been approved.
$4.8 billion of available capital, no debt, and a $0.44 quarterly dividend.
verdict: Franco-Nevada is the landlord of gold mines: it doesn't dig, it just collects. This quarter the rent went up because gold did, while the tenants shipped fewer ounces. A profit beat on a revenue miss, and the stock barely blinked.
